events.title: National Carousel Day
events.description:
@

National Carousel Day

Saturday, July 25 from 12pm–3pm

Featuring our Antique Children’s Carousel on National Carousel Day!

  • Roaming Magician
  • Balloon Twister
  • Unlimited carousel rides for smaller guests

Carousel and entertainment on 3rd Floor, near Toddler Town. Included with General Admission or Member Pass.

Celebrate National Carousel Day with us and the colorful characters on our Antique Children’s Carousel!

On Saturday, July 25 from 12pm-3pm, we’ll have plenty of magic, balloon animals, and carnival music just for the occasion. Smaller guests (under 54″ tall) can take a ride on our menagerie of enchanting animals, and then saunter over to the Artifacts gift shop to check out our Zebra Carousel shirts in youth sizes.

This beautifully restored, 20-foot diameter carousel was originally manufactured in the 1920s by the renowned Allan Herschell Company of North Tonawanda, New York, the most prolific carousel maker in American history. Known for producing more than 3,000 hand-carved wooden carousels, the company specialized in portable machines that traveled with carnivals across the country, bringing joy to generations of families.

In 1988, the carousel was restored as a historical art preservation project by local sculptor Carlos Sardina and his wife Judy. The Sardinas toured their carousels nationwide from the late 1980s through the early 2010s, sharing the joy of antique rides with communities across the country.

Carousel and entertainment on 3rd Floor, near Toddler Town. Included with General Admission or Member Pass. Children must be under 54″ tall to ride. Children under 40″ tall can ride with a parent or guardian.

events.description:

Buy Tickets

Friday, September 18 from 7pm–11pm

Grab your dirndl or lederhosen and put on your dancing shoes, because it’s time to kick off the Fall season with one of the world’s oldest drinks and Bavaria’s greatest tradition — Oktoberfest!

“Why is it in September if it’s called Oktoberfest?” Great question! Although the event started with a celebration of King Ludwig’s wedding in October 1810, local wars, epidemics, recessions, weather, and other influences have pushed it around the calendar over its 200+ year history. Oktoberfest also absorbed some of the late-Summer/early-Fall agricultural celebrations around the harvest season, and the modern event in Munich is now scheduled almost entirely in September, ending the first weekend of October.

Explore hidden corners, sip seasonal brews, and raise a toast with local Oompah band ÜberCool in one of the most unique venues in the city!

Welcome to Fright at the Museum!

Step into a world of spine-tingling wonder at our one-of-a-kind, all-ages Halloween celebration! Prepare to be amazed, mystified, and thoroughly entertained as you embark on a journey through a realm of oddities and curiosities that will leave you both thrilled and captivated.

Fright-tastic Exhibits


Jack-O-Lanterns, Skeletons, Spiders, and plenty of creeping, crawling decorations on every floor!

Doc Terminus’ Odditorium

3rd Floor – Architecture Hall

Follow the skeletons to the 3rd Floor, where you’ll find Doc Terminus and his extraordinary crew of misfits hard at work in the Odditorium. Somewhere between inexplicable and amazing, witness a variety show beyond compare featuring flaming swords, spectacular sideshows performances, and a few more spooky surprises to keep you on the edge of your seat!

As our building approaches its 100th birthday, a few of the former residents decided to visit the old haunting ground.

Hauntings:

The Organist’s Awakening

Enchanted Caves

The St. Louis Theatre Organ Society’s haunting ballads play on our beautifully restored 1924 Wurlitzer Theatre Organ that was rebuilt directly into the walls of the Enchanted Caves. Reverberating from the cement stalagmites on the 1st Floor to the Rooftop skylight shining down from the 11th, the song of The Organist will sonically serenade your eardrums and rattle your bones!

Not-So-Spooky Storytelling

4th Floor – Sullivan Gallery

Join the City Museum Witch for some not-so-spooky stories and tales of triumph for all ages! Pillows, blankets, and rugs for the littler ones to get cozy; benches and bathrooms nearby for the bigger ones to take a break.

Showtimes:
Sat: 11:00am – 2:00pm
Sun: 11:00am – 2:00pm

Coven & Cauldron

1st Floor – Cabin Inn Bar

Enter a world of magic, mystery, and a dash of the macabre at Coven & Cauldron – the ultimate witches’ pub experience! Elevate your experience with our enchanting concoction, a Poison Apple cocktail, for this is where the supernatural and the extraordinary converge.

Vampire Bar

3rd Floor – Cowboy Bar

Step into the shadows and immerse yourself in the allure of the night where darkness and decadence intertwine! Indulge in the mystique of ancient lore and blood-thirsty beasts as you enter a realm of intoxicating ambiance and tantalizing flavors. Sip on a rich, crimson True Blood cocktail or take a terrifyingly terrific Zombie Shot to be transported to a world where mortals and immortals coexist.

Mad Scientist’s Lab

3rd Floor – Beatnik Bob’s

Ignore those warning signs and radiation dials and enter the Mad Scientist’s Lab! Step into a world of flickering control panels, uranium-green glow, and test chambers filled with classified concoctions. Enjoy a Fall Old Fashioned while you peruse the cute but creepy ceramic creatures of Eerie Baby, or try something a little more basic with a PSL White Russian… just don’t tell the Mad Scientist, or he might go nuclear!

Slightly Possessed Spirits

One sip and you’ll feel the shiver of something otherworldly!

🍎 Poison Apple – Vodka, Midori, lime juice, and apple juice

🧟‍♂️ Zombie Shot – Malibu, Midori, and pineapple juice, served in a giant syringe

🩸 True Blood – Tequila, triple sec, strawberry puree, passionfruit juice, and margarita mix, served in a blood bag

🍂 Fall Old Fashioned – Jameson, pumpkin purée, cinnamon and nutmeg simple syrups, bitters, and club soda, garnished with a cinnamon stick

🎃 PSL White Russian – Vodka, Kahlua, pumpkin spiced Irish cream, pumpkin puree, and heavy cream, garnished with a cinnamon stick

Whether you’re a thrill-seeker, a curious explorer, or simply someone who revels in the extraordinary, Fright at the Museum promises a month of entertainment that will send shivers down your spine. Bring your friends, family, or dare to venture solo – this is an experience that will unite all who seek the unknown and revel in the unusual!

Get ready Transylvanians — It’s time for The Rocky Horror Picture Show!

SOLD OUT!

This spooky season, join us for a late-night screening of The Rocky Horror Picture Show on the Rooftop with LIVE shadowcast Flustered Mustard. Eager to do The Time Warp? Great! We can’t wait to have you! Never seen it? Throw on your mother’s high heels and fishnets, ’cause you’re in for a treat!

The longest-running midnight movie of all time stars Tim Curry as the kinky yet endearing “transsexual from Transylvania” Dr. Frank N. Furter, Susan Sarandon and Barry Bostwick as his hapless guests Brad and Janet, Meat Loaf as motorcycle-riding rough trade and author Richard O’Brien as the hunchbacked butler Riff Raff. It’s harmless musical fun—a delightful spoof of Hollywood horror movies and Old Dark House melodramas. Become a part of the movie by shouting out lines with the cast as well as throwing props to mock the action on screen. The Rocky Horror Picture Show was the first—and is still the best—interactive movie experience!

Dressing up is HIGHLY encouraged! Rocky Horror isn’t Rocky Horror without the corsets and lipstick.

Each ticket includes a Prop Bag (a $5 value) with all the necessary items for the evening. For the safety of everyone involved, outside Prop Bags will NOT be allowed at the screening. Bag checks will happen at the door, so please use common sense (dangerous items will not be allowed in). The cast will have a whole slew of t-shirts, stickers, buttons, and other items for sale as well.

  • Drinks and food will be available for purchase

  • Live pre-show begins at 8pm

  • Lots of time before and after the film to enjoy the Rooftop

events.title: Pumpkin Throw Down
events.description:
@

Get out your gourds — Halloween is over, and it’s time to throw out those old pumpkins!

Pumpkin spice? Too basic. Pumpkin pie? Delicious, but no. Pumpkin chuckin? That’s right, this City Museum fall tradition is back! Gather up all of your pumpkins, gourds, squash, and any other vegetables you’ve carved a face onto… and throw them off the side of our building!

Sunday, November 1 from 12pm–3pm on 10th Floor Balcony

Eckert’s Farm has provided a limited number of pumpkins to get us started, but otherwise it’s BYOP — Bring Your Own Pumpkin! Follow us up to the 10th floor, where our team will lead you to the Launch Pad just outside the north banquet hall. From there, you call the shots, as you chuck your pumpkins off the building and try to hit the target in our parking lot to win some Weirdly Wonderful prizes.

New Earth Farms will be composting our pumpkins (or whatever is left of them) after the event, and they can NOT include any inorganic material, such as paint, glitter, or stickers.

General Admission or Member Pass required.
